slots.name: Christy Hoffman
slots.bio:
Christy Hoffman was a four-year letterwinner and starting goalkeeper for the University of Cincinnati women's soccer program from 1997 to 2001, a defining figure during the program's ascent in Conference USA. A Cincinnati native out of McAuley High School, Hoffman arrived in Clifton as a true freshman in 1997 and immediately set the program's single-season shutout record — a mark that announced both the player and the rising profile of UC women's soccer.

Across her career between the posts she earned multiple Conference USA all-conference selections and top defensive player recognition in 2001, finishing her career ranked 4th all-time at UC in career shutouts (13.5 through her junior season). Her defensive consistency anchored a program that became a perennial postseason contender in the late 1990s and early 2000s.

Off the field, Hoffman authored an even more historic first. In 2001 she became the first CoSIDA Academic All-America selection in University of Cincinnati women's soccer history, pairing elite athletic performance with classroom excellence in a way no Bearcat women's soccer player had before. Her induction into the 2026 James P. Kelly Sr. Athletics Hall of Fame recognizes both the records she set in goal and the academic standard she established for every Bearcat who has followed.

slots.name: Al Lanier
slots.bio: One of UC's track and field all-time greats who garnered a total of five All-Amereican awards. First Bearcat trickster to qualify for the NCAA Championships in all four seasons, competing in both the long jump and triple jump at the outdoor championships. Earned All-American honors as a junior with a third place finish in the triple jump. Capped his career by capturing All-American plaudits in both the lone jump (second place) and triple jump (sixth) as a senior. Also qualified for the NCAA Indoor Championships in the long jump and triple jump his junior and senior campaigns, garnering All-American honors each year in the triple jump. Closed his career holding UC records in both the long jump (26'1 1/2") and triple jump (55'6 1/2"). Narrowly missed earning a berth on the U.S. Olympic Team at the 1972 Trials. Competed on the U.S. Army team that made a tour of China in 1975. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1988.

slots.name: Paulette Angilecchia
slots.bio: Starred at UC from 1993-1996. Three-time All-Conference USA selection. Ranks 3rd in both points(118) and goals(50) and 6th in assists(18) in a season at UC. Twice named to the Conference USA Commissioner's Honor Roll.

slots.name: Phil Meyers
slots.bio: Four-season letterwinner in football. Three-time All-Ohio selection as the right end. Later selected by a panel of sportswriters to UC's All-Time Football Team. Active on campus as a member of the Sigma Sigma honorary and the Sigma Alpha Mue Fraternity. Served on the UC Board of Trustees in the 1950s. Successful builder and developer in the Cincinnati area who was well-known for his philanthropic work. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1977.

slots.name: Dr. Richard Bryant
slots.bio: All-around student-athlete and campus leader. Lettered in football, basketball and track. Served as senior class president, student government vice president, was active in fraternities and social organizations and earned election to Phi Beta Kappa, Cincinnatus Society and Sigma Sigma. Completed his medical degree and served on the staffs of area hospitals while a member of UC's College of Medicine staff. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1984.

slots.name: Roger McClendon
slots.bio: Considered UC's player of the decade for the 1980s. Four-year starter who led the team in scoring in each of his first three campaigns. Closed his career as UC's No. 2 career scorer with 1,789 points. Two-time first team All-Metro Conference selection. Team MVP as a junior. Co-captain as a senior. As devoted to academics as he was basketball, completed his degree in engineering. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1998.

slots.name: Elbie Nickel
slots.bio: One of UC's top players of the 1940s and the prototype of a productive tight end. Played on the 1940-41-42 UC teams before entering the service for World War II. Returned to UC following the war to complete his academic and athletic career. Captain of the 1946 team that upset defending Big Ten champion Indiana, a game in which he scored a touchdown and kicked a field goal. Helped UC to a 9-2 record in 1946, capped with an 18-6 win over Virginia Tech in the Sun Bowl, UC's first bowl appearance. Also lettered in basketball and baseball. Played 11 seasons in the NFL with the Pittsburgh Steelers, later earning a selection to the all-time Steelers team at tight end. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1982.

slots.name: Jim Kelly Jr.
slots.bio: Earned the reputation as one of the top receivers in UC grid history during his four seasons. Either shared or owned seven UC receiving records when he concluded his career--records that were broken by receivers he tutored ( UC Hall of Famers Jim O'Brien and Tom Rossley) in the late 1960s as UC's receivers coach. As a junior, he finished sixth nationally in receptions with 42. Leading scorer in the Mid-American Conference in 1950 with nine TD receptions and one PAT kick. Returned to UC as assistant coach in 1960 and served for 16 seasons under five head coaches, coaching receivers and kickers. Launched his administrative career as assistant athletics director in 1977. Closed his career with 82 receptions for 1,114 yards. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1978.

slots.name: Tony Trabert
slots.bio: NCAA Singles Champion 1951, runner-up in doubles (partner Bob Molt). Starting guard on the 1951 Bearcat basketball team that participated in the National Invitation Tournament). Member of the United States Davis Cup teams, 1951-55. Compiled a 26-8 Davis Cup record. Captain of five U.S. Davis Cup teams (1953, 1976-80). No. 1 singles player on the 1954 Davis Cup team that won the cup back from the Australians. U.S. Championships (later known as the U.S. Open) singles champion twice (1953, 1955). U.S. Championships doubles champion (1954). Wimbledon singles champion (1955). Wimbledon doubles runner-up (1954). French Open singles champion twice (1954, 1955). French Open doubles champion (1950; partner Bill Talbert), (1954, 1955; partner Vic Seixas). Italian Open doubles champion (1950; partner Bill Talbert), runner-up (1954). Italian Open mixed doubles champion (1954). Australian Open doubles champion (1955; partner Vic Seixas). Sigma Sigma and ULEX member at UC. Ranked USLTA Singles top 10 four times, reaching No. 1 in 1953 and 1955. National Indoor Junior singles and doubles champion (1948). National Clay Court singles champion twice (1951, 1955). National Clay Court doubles champion three times (1951, 1954, 1955). United States Hardcourt singles champion (1954); doubles champion (1950, 1953). National Indoor singles and doubles champion (1955). World Pro doubles champion (1956). World Pro Singles runner-up (1960). William Howard Taft Medal for Notable Achievement from the UC alumni (1994). Named to the Hamilton County Hall of Fame (1968), the National Lawn Tennis Hall of Fame (1970), the College Tennis Hall of Fame (1983), and the Cincinnati Tennis Hall of Fame (2002). UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1977.

slots.name: Kara Molony
slots.bio:
Kara Molony stands as the most decorated and dominant figure in the history of University of Cincinnati women’s tennis. Arriving on campus in the mid-1990s, Molony immediately transformed the program, blending an aggressive baseline game with an unmatched competitive spirit. Throughout her four-year tenure from 1996 to 2000, she redefined the standards of excellence for UC tennis, becoming the first player in program history to earn First Team All-Conference honors in four consecutive seasons. Her impact was felt instantaneously as she earned Conference USA Freshman of the Year honors in 1997, leading the Bearcats to a runner-up finish in the conference tournament.

During her junior campaign in 1998-99, Molony reached the pinnacle of individual success, winning a staggering 37 singles matches. This record-breaking season solidified her reputation as one of the premier players in the Midwest and helped elevate Cincinnati’s profile on the national collegiate circuit. Her prowess was not limited to singles play; Molony was a versatile tactician on the doubles court, eventually becoming the only player in program history to surpass the century mark in both singles and doubles career victories. Her leadership on the court served as the backbone for the Bearcats' competitiveness during a period of significant growth for the athletics department.

Beyond her athletic dominance, Molony was the quintessential student-athlete, embodying the highest values of the University. She was a three-time ITA Scholar-Athlete and was named the UC Female Student-Athlete of the Year in 2000, an honor that recognized her holistic contribution to the university community. Her academic rigor, combined with her relentless work ethic on the courts of the Trabert-Talbert Tennis Center, set a benchmark for future generations of Bearcats.

Kara Molony’s induction into the James P. Kelly Athletics Hall of Fame in 2021 serves as a testament to a career defined by longevity, excellence, and historic statistical achievement. As the program's all-time leader in nearly every major statistical category, her legacy remains the gold standard for Cincinnati tennis. She remains one of the few athletes in school history to dominate their respective sport so thoroughly that their records have remained largely untouched for over two decades.

slots.name: Mike Whiting
slots.bio: Four-year starter and all-time leading scorer in soccer. Established UC single game records for goals (4), assists (4) and points (10) which stand today. Is UC's career leader in points (115) and assists (31) and is second in goals (42). Earned All-Ohio honors in each of his four seasons. Named to the All-Mideast Team his junior and senior campaigns. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1990.

slots.name: Eddie Coons
slots.bio: Lettered in four sports--football, basketball, baseball and track. Earned All-Ohio honors in both football and basketball. Served as team captain of the basketball and baseball teams as a senior. Outstanding baseball prospect who declined a number of professional offers to enter business with Cincinnati Bell. Returned to UC to serve as Athletics Ticket Manager. Member of the UC Athletic Hall of Fame charter class of inductees.

slots.name: Tom Blake
slots.bio: Stalwart offensive lineman on the successful UC teams of the late 1940s. After playing as a freshman at Tennessee during World War II, he joined the UC varsity in 1946 and became the starting left tackle on the team that posted a 9-2 record and defeated Virginia Tech in the Sun Bowl. Switched to right tackle for his final two seasons and earned a reputation for his hard-nosed play. Team captain as a senior. Inducted into the Sigma Sigma honorary. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1998.

slots.name: Tom O'Malley
slots.bio: Four-year letterman, three-year starter. Ranked among the nation's top 10 leading passers as a junior in 1948. Led the nation in passing yardage (1,617) in 1949, passing for 16 touchdowns. Inserted into the game vs. Miami University as a freshman and fired a touchdown pass that clinched the 13-7 victory and sent UC to the Sun Bowl, its first bowl appearance. Jersey number 27 retired when he concluded his career. UC Athletics Hall of Fame 2006.

Cole's induction into the James P. Kelly UC Athletics Hall of Fame stands as a testament to his enduring legacy and the profound regard with which he is held by the University. slots.name: Madinah Slaise
slots.bio:
Madina Slaise etched her name into the University of Cincinnati's women's basketball history, culminating in her induction into the James P. Kelly Hall of Fame in 2016. Slaise was a pivotal figure for the Bearcats during her collegiate career, playing from 1996 to 2000. Her time on the court coincided with a significant period for the program, contributing to a foundation of competitive excellence that resonated throughout the conference and beyond.

Her induction into the James P. Kelly Hall of Fame in 2016 serves as a testament to her enduring influence and the respect she garnered from her coaches, teammates, and the Cincinnati athletic community. This honor acknowledges not just her prowess as a player, but also her role in upholding the proud traditions of Bearcat athletics. Madina Slaise stands as a truly deserving member of this esteemed group, forever a part of the University of Cincinnati's rich athletic tapestry.

slots.name: Robert Miller
slots.bio: Four-year regular who helped lead UC to three NCAA Tournament appearances, two Metro Conference championships and a 90-27 record. An 8.9-point scorer as a freshman, he scored at a 17.3-point clip in the NCAA Tournament to earn Midwest Regional all-tournament honors. Garnered Bearcat MVP honors his sophomore and junior seasons, during which he was the squad's scoring and rebounding leader. Second-leading scorer and top rebounder and shot blocker as a senior. Became the fourth Bearcat to top the 1,000 plateau in both points (1,498) and rebounds (1,060). Second team All-Metro Conference pick his junior and senior years. Honorable mention All-American as a senior in 1978 (AP). Taken in the fourth round by Phoenix in the 1978 NBA draft to begin a six-season NBA career. UC Athletics Hall of Fame 1999.

slots.name: Gene Rossi
slots.bio: Three-year starter and team passing leader. Topped the 1,000-yard mark in passing in each of his three seasons. Concluded his career as UC's all-time leader in passes attempted (492), completions (257), completion percentage (.522), passing yards (4,003) and TD passes (37), all of which still rank him among the Bearcat leaders. Led UC to a 26-6-1 record as a starter. Three-time All-Mid-American Conference selection. Earned All-Ohio honors his junior and senior seasons. Honorable mention All-American in both 1951 (Colliers) and 1952 (AP, UPI, Colliers). Jersey number (28) retired. Selected by Baltimore in the 1953 NFL draft but played professionally in Canada. UC Athletics Hall of Fame 1984.

slots.name: Ralph Davis
slots.bio: Three-year starter for the UC teams of the late 1950s that compiled a 79-9 record, won three Missouri Valley Conference titles and made two appearances in the NCAA Final Four, finishing third each time. Co-captain as a senior. High-scoring performer whose talents were overshadowed by Oscar Robertson. Second on the team in scoring and assists his final two seasons, averaging 15.5 points per game as a junior. Was No. 6 on the UC career scoring list when he closed his career with 1,093 points. Earned second team All-American honors as a senior in 1960 (Converse). Taken in the third round of the 1960 NBA draft by Cincinnati. UC Athletics Hall of Fame 1981.

slots.name: Wayne Mason
slots.bio:
Wayne Mason is one of the foundational hurdle figures in University of Cincinnati track and field history. Competing for the Bearcats from 1977 through 1980, Mason earned First-Team All-America honors in the 110m hurdles in 1980, finishing third at the NCAA Outdoor Championships — a podium finish that places him among an exclusive group of Bearcat track and field athletes.

A four-time NCAA Championship qualifier across his career — in the 60-yard high hurdles indoors in 1977, 1978 and 1979, and in the 110m hurdles outdoors in 1980 — Mason was the rare athlete who consistently advanced to nationals in an era when getting there was harder than at almost any time in NCAA history.

His record-book footprint remains visible more than four decades later. Mason still holds the UC indoor 55m hurdles hand-timed record (7.1) and the fully automatic timed record (7.34), both set in 1979, and his 13.60 outdoor 110m hurdles mark from 1980 still ranks No. 3 all-time in the UC record book, behind only Terrence Somerville and Olympic medalist David Payne. The 2026 induction into the James P. Kelly Sr. Athletics Hall of Fame is overdue recognition for a historical-era Bearcat whose marks have outlasted the careers of nearly every athlete who has chased them.

Sean Kilpatrick's time at Cincinnati was more than just a series of games; it was a defining chapter in the program's narrative, one that continues to resonate with fans and aspiring athletes alike.

slots.name: Stephanie Niemer
slots.bio: 2011: Serves as the Student Assistant coach for the 2011 season. After a very successful Bearcat career, Niemer will help all hitters and assist in video and stats. She will graduate in December of 2011. Niemer's Career Stats. 2010 Match-by-Match Stats. 2009 Match-by-Match Stats. 2008 Match-by-Match Stats. 2007 Match-by-Match Stats.

slots.name: Jason Fabini
slots.bio: Three-time first team All-Conference USA selection. Team co-captain. Lettered al four years at UC. Played in 44 games throughout his career making 43 starts. Rated as the 20th best senior in the country in 1997 by NFL Draft expert Mel Kiper. 1996 recipient of the John Pease Award as the team's top offensive lineman.

slots.name: Steve Collier
slots.bio: Mr. Basketball for the state of Indiana as a high school senior lived up to all expectations beginning with his freshman season. Was named team captain as a freshman and helped lead the team to a 23-6 record and a regional finish in the NCAA Tournament. Showed his versatility, surrendering the point guard responsibilities his sophomore and junior campaigns to junior college newcomer Gary Yoder. Played in 114 games, making 104 starts. Member of UC's 1,000-point scorers club (1,252). Earned honorable mention All-Metro Conference honors his junior and senior seasons. Was an honorable mention All-American in 1976 (Street & Smith's). UC Athletic Hall of Fame 2000.

slots.name: Nick Skorich
slots.bio: Three-year letterman in football as a rugged two-way lineman. Team captain as a senior. Earned All-Ohio honors and honorable mention All-American mention as a senior. Played three seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers. Launched his coaching career in the NFL with Pittsburgh and served at Green Bay; was offensive coordinator for the 1961 NFL champion Philadelphia Eagles and defensive coordinator for the 1964 NFL champion Cleveland Browns. Served as head coach of the Philadelphia Eagles (three years) and Cleveland Browns (four years). Was Assistant Supervisor of Officials for the NFL. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1977.

slots.name: Ron Bonham
slots.bio: Starter throughout his three-year varsity career, helping UC compile a record of 72-13 during that period. Helped lead UC to the NCAA National Championship as a sophomore in 1962 and a runner-up finish in 1963. Leading scorer his junior and senior seasons, posting averages of 21.0 and 24.4. Closed his career as UC's second-leading scorer of all-time with 1,666 points, a total which currently ranks him in the top 10. His 19.6-point career scoring average is the third-best in UC history. Three-time All-Missouri Valley Conference selection. Team captain as a senior. Consensus first team All-American in 1963 (AP, UPI, Basketball Writers, Helms, Converse, NABC), third team pick (NEA); earned second team All-American honors in 1964 (AP, UPI, Converse) and was third team (NABC). Columbus Touchdown Club Player of the Year selection in 1963. Taken in the second round by Boston in the 1964 NBA Draft and played on two NBA championship teams for the Celtics. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1986.

slots.bio:

Kelly Athletics Hall of Fame in 2023 serves as a testament to a distinguished career that left an indelible mark on the Bearcats' Men's Track & Field program. slots.name: Ray Nolting
slots.bio: Three-year starter at halfback in football. Three-time All-Buckeye Athletic Association selection. Earned All-Ohio honors in both his junior and senior seasons. Helped UC compile a 20-6-1 record and win two conference titles during his three seasons. Honorable mention All-American in 1935. Drafted by Chicago and played eight seasons in the NFL. Returned to serve as head coach at UC, 1946-48, directing the Bearcats to their first bowl appearance and a 23-15-1 ledger. Member of the UC Athletic Hall of Fame charter class of inductees.

slots.name: Sonja Jackson
slots.bio: Three time team Most Valuable Player. Earned first team All-Metro Conference honors her junior and senior seasons. Finished 11th nationally in kills as a junior. Became the first Bearcat to record 1,000 career kills and 1,000 career digs. Ranked among UC's best in seven categories. Played pivotal role in the turnaround of the program, that after managing just 14 wins over two seasons, had a 16-win year her junior campaign and posted a 27-8 ledger her senior year. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 2002.

slots.name: Joe Linneman
slots.bio: Four-sport letterwinner, earning honors in football, basketball, baseball and track. Achieved the most success in football where he was a standout at four different positions during his career. Served as team captain as a senior. Honored for his accomplishments as a punter. Went on to play professional football. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1990.

slots.name: Bob Huggins
slots.bio: Bob Huggins coached the University of Cincinnati men's basketball program from 1989 to 2005, posting a 399–127 record and turning the Bearcats into a national power. Under Huggins, UC reached the 1992 NCAA Final Four, won multiple conference titles, and made 14 straight NCAA Tournament appearances. A National Basketball Hall of Fame inductee (2022), Huggins is one of the most accomplished coaches in college basketball history.

slots.name: Bev Obringer
slots.bio: Dominant post player during her four-plus seasons as a Bearcat. Showed the ability to be a force inside as an alternate in the starting lineup during her freshman year. Emerged to lead the squad in rebounding (9.4) as a sophomore. Missed all but the first two games of the 1987 season due to injury but came back to lead the team in both scoring and rebounding in 1988 and 1989, averaging 17.4 points and 9.1 rebounds as a senior. First team All-Metro Conference her junior and senior years, also earning all-tournament honors in both seasons. Earned honorable mention All-American honors in 1986 (American Women's Sports Federation). UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1999.

slots.name: Dr. Nancy Hamant
slots.bio: The Nancy Hamant Academics Center was officially dedicated in a private ceremony on August 3, 2006 in the Richard E. Lindner Athletics Center. Named for Faculty Athletics Representative Dr. Nancy R. Hamant, the Academics Center gives student-athletes a variety of ways to fulfill their classwork needs. Housed on the fifth floor of the Lindner Athletics Center, the center includes a study room with 34 work areas, 14 tutoring rooms, five group meeting rooms and a 71-station computer lab. Hamant, in her 21st year as faculty representative, holds three University of Cincinnati degrees. She received a bachelor's in Arts & Sciences in 1957, added her master's in Education in 1961and earned her PhD from the College of Education in 1967. She joined the UC faculty in 1964 and is currently an Associate Professor and Coordinator of Professional Experiences in the College of Education. A member of the NCAA Postgraduate Scholarship Committee, Athletics Policy and Planning Committee and a liaison with the NCAA and BIG EAST Conference, Hamant is a former president of the UC Alumni Association. Hamant and her husband, Tom, are George Smith Society Members and dedicated season-ticket holders. The Hamants made a substantial gift to the Varsity Village project and plan gift from their estate, establishing the Nancy R. and Thomas H. Hamant endowment fund.

slots.name: Pat Cummings
slots.bio: Set new standards for big men at UC. Closed his career as the No. 2 scorer in UC history with 1,762 points (total currently sixth). Also owned the career mark for field goal percentage (.581), which has since been topped once. Season field goal percentage of .642 set in 1978 remains a UC record. Became a starter his sophomore season and relinquished the role only when sidelined for most of the 1977 season by a fractured ankle. Led the team in scoring his junior and senior seasons, averaging 24.4 points as a senior. Team MVP his junior and senior seasons and tri-captain as a senior. Two-time All-Metro Conference first team selection and league Player of the Year as a senior. Earned All-American recognition as a senior in 1979 (Citizens Savings). Taken in the third round of the 1979 NBA draft by Milwaukee. Played 10 seasons in the NBA. UC Athletics Hall of Fame in 1990.

slots.name: Dr. William Schwarberg
slots.bio: Outstanding running back on the UC football teams of the mid-1930s and also starred in baseball. Following service in the Navy during World War II, he returned to UC and served in just about every capacity in the athletics department until retiring in 1982. Served as head golf coach for 28 years, during which he compiled a 257-69 record in dual meets and developed three NCAA Championships qualifiers. Never had a losing season as head golf coach, at one time posting 47 consecutive victories. Also served stints as head baseball coach, director of intramurals and associate athletic director. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1985.

slots.name: Mardy Gilyard
slots.bio:
Mardy Gilyard, a dynamic figure who indelibly impacted the University of Cincinnati football program, proudly takes his place among the university's athletic legends as a 2024 inductee into the James P. Kelly UC Athletics Hall of Fame. His electrifying presence on the field captivated fans and inspired teammates, embodying the spirit of competitive excellence that defines Bearcat athletics. Gilyard's induction celebrates not only his remarkable contributions but also his lasting legacy as a pivotal player during a significant era for the program.

A standout during his time in Clifton, Gilyard consistently demonstrated a versatile skillset that made him a formidable force. Whether as a receiver challenging opposing secondaries or as a return specialist igniting rallies, his athleticism and tenacity were undeniable. Gilyard's play was often a catalyst, providing crucial moments of brilliance that propelled the Bearcats to national prominence and etched his name into the hearts of the UC faithful. His commitment to excellence set a high standard, contributing to the competitive atmosphere that continues to define the program.

Beyond the statistical achievements, Gilyard's impact resonated deeply within the team and the university community. He was a leader whose dedication and passion served as an example for his peers, fostering a culture of success and determination. His Hall of Fame recognition is a testament to the profound influence he wielded, solidifying his status as one of the most memorable athletes to don the red and black. His storied career at Cincinnati continues to inspire new generations of Bearcat athletes.

Mardy Gilyard's induction into the James P. Kelly UC Athletics Hall of Fame is a fitting tribute to a player whose talent and spirit left an undeniable mark on the University of Cincinnati. His legacy is one of thrilling performances, unwavering dedication, and a significant contribution to the rich tapestry of Bearcat football history. His name will forever be synonymous with an era of excellence, celebrated for bringing excitement and prestige to the institution.

slots.name: Dr. Ken Stephens
slots.bio:
Kenneth Stephens, a celebrated contributor to the University of Cincinnati's athletic landscape, earned a well-deserved induction into the James P. Kelly Hall of Fame in 2014. His recognition as a "Contributor" speaks volumes about the breadth and depth of his impact, signifying a legacy built not on individual athletic statistics, but on the foundational support, unwavering dedication, and visionary efforts that elevate an entire athletic program. Stephens' induction reflects a profound understanding by the Hall of Fame committee of the myriad ways individuals can shape the trajectory of collegiate sports, extending beyond the competitive field or court.

Stephens' contributions, while not chronicled in traditional points or victories, were nonetheless integral to the flourishing of UC Athletics. His efforts likely spanned crucial areas such as fundraising, strategic planning, facility development, or fostering a supportive environment for student-athletes. Inductees in the Contributor category embody the spirit of sustained commitment and often work behind the scenes, yet their influence reverberates throughout the institution, enabling countless athletes to achieve their potential and enriching the broader university community. His inclusion in this esteemed group underscores the belief that true success in collegiate athletics is a collective endeavor, built on the passion and dedication of many individuals like Kenneth Stephens.

The James P. Kelly Hall of Fame exists to honor those who have left an indelible mark on the University of Cincinnati's athletic tradition. Kenneth Stephens' induction in 2014 firmly establishes his place within this distinguished pantheon of individuals whose commitment and contributions have fortified the legacy of the Bearcats. His recognition serves as an enduring testament to his significant role in shaping the athletic programs, providing an example of leadership and dedication that continues to inspire future generations of Cincinnati athletes and supporters.

slots.name: Dottie Mueller Braun
slots.plaque_sport_line: BASKETBALL · SWIMMING · RIFLE · ARCHERY · VOLLEYBALL · BOWLING
slots.bio: Distinguished herself both as an outstanding student and fine athlete while in the campus' women's sports programs of the late 1940s. Participated actively in six sports: basketball, swimming, rifle, archery, volleyball and bowling. Earned a UC Blazer, the highest women's athletic award, at the conclusion of her sophomore year. Member of Phi Beta Kappa and Mortar Board. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1981.

slots.name: Greg Cook
slots.bio: One of the nation's most prolific passers of the 1960s. Led the nation in completions (219), passing yards (3,272), total offense (3,210) and touchdowns (25) in 1968. Closed his career as UC's career record-holder for completions (332), attempts (655), passing yards (4,906), and TD passes (34). Set an NCAA record for passing yards in a game with 554 vs. Ohio in 1968. Second team All-American in 1968 (Central Press), also earning honorable mention All-American recognition (AP, UPI, NEA). MVP of the College All-Star Game. Played in the Blue-Gray, American Bowl and Senior Bowl all-star games. Taken with the No. 5 pick by the Cincinnati Bengals in the 1969 draft. Led the American Football Conference in passing and earned Rookie of the Year honors in 1969. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1986. UC Football Ring of Honor.

slots.name: Jim Holstein
slots.bio: Three-sport star of the early 1950s. Led the basketball team in scoring in each of his final three seasons and closed his career at UC's all-time scoring leader (1,146 points). Earned All-Mid-American Conference honors in each of his final three seasons. MVP of the 1951-52 Bearcats. Selected by Minneapolis in the 1952 NBA Draft. Lettered in football and was a standout in baseball. Served stints as a college head basketball coach at St. Joseph's and Ball State. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1980.

slots.name: Jacqueline Keire
slots.bio:
Jacqueline Keire's induction into the James P. Kelly UC Athletics Hall of Fame in 2022 stands as a testament to a career defined by dedication and excellence within the Women's Swimming & Diving program. Her presence in the pool was a significant fixture, contributing to an era of growth and competitive spirit for the Bearcats. Through relentless training and an unwavering commitment to her sport, Keire exemplified the ideals of a student-athlete, leaving an indelible mark on the University of Cincinnati's athletic lineage.

While specific statistical records of her achievements may not be readily available, Keire's impact transcends mere numbers. Her induction recognizes a legacy built on consistent performance and a profound dedication to her team. She was a pivotal figure in shaping the identity of the Women's Swimming & Diving program during her time, inspiring teammates and future generations of Bearcats to pursue athletic and academic distinction. The Hall of Fame honor reflects not only her individual prowess but also the collective spirit she fostered within the program.

Jacqueline Keire's place in the James P. Kelly UC Athletics Hall of Fame permanently enshrines her contributions to the University of Cincinnati. This prestigious recognition celebrates a career characterized by exceptional commitment and a profound influence on her sport. Her legacy serves as an enduring source of inspiration, embodying the spirit of competitive drive and the pursuit of excellence that defines Bearcat athletics.

slots.name: Jim Stanley
slots.bio:
Jim Stanley stands as a testament to the era of the versatile, multi-sport endurance athlete at the University of Cincinnati. Competing during the transition into the early 1960s, Stanley was a foundational member of the Bearcats' distance running programs, earning a total of six varsity letters across three different sports. His dedication to the grueling disciplines of Cross Country and Track & Field helped elevate UC's profile within the Missouri Valley Conference, establishing a standard of grit and consistency that would define the program for decades to come.

During his tenure on the cross country trails, Stanley was known for his tactical intelligence and steady scoring, often serving as the vital link that secured team victories in dual meets. His ability to maintain a high-level performance across the autumn cross country season and the spring track season made him an indispensable asset to the coaching staff. Stanley’s athletic range was further demonstrated by his participation in Field Hockey, a rarity for male athletes of the time, which highlighted his exceptional agility and competitive drive beyond the running paths.

Beyond his statistical contributions, Stanley’s legacy at the University of Cincinnati is marked by his lifelong commitment to the university community and his embodiment of the 'student-athlete' ideal. His induction into the James P. Kelly Athletics Hall of Fame in 2021 served as a long-overdue recognition of a pioneer who helped bridge the gap between UC’s early athletic history and its modern successes. He remains a revered figure among the alumni, remembered for his endurance, versatility, and the quiet dignity with which he represented the Red and Black.

slots.name: Tony Pike
slots.bio:
Tony Pike, a name synonymous with a golden era of Cincinnati Bearcats football, rightfully takes his place among the university's legends as an inductee into the James P. Kelly Hall of Fame in 2025. Pike's tenure under center redefined expectations and brought unprecedented national attention to the UC program. His impact transcended individual statistics, elevating the entire team to a level of consistent competitiveness and championship contention previously unseen. He led with poise and a remarkable understanding of the game, becoming a true leader for some of the most dynamic offenses in Bearcats history.

Pike's journey at Cincinnati was marked by a steady progression, culminating in seasons that captivated the college football landscape. His ability to connect with receivers, extend plays, and make crucial throws in high-pressure situations endeared him to the Bearcats faithful. Beyond his play on the field, Pike exemplified the student-athlete ideal, embodying the dedication and character that the university strives to instill in its young men and women. His leadership was not just about wins and losses; it was about fostering a culture of excellence and a belief in what was possible.

The 2025 Hall of Fame induction recognizes Pike's indelible mark on the University of Cincinnati's athletic heritage. He represents a pivotal figure in the evolution of Bearcats football, a testament to what disciplined effort and a winning mentality can achieve. His legacy continues to inspire current and future generations of UC athletes, serving as a reminder of the potent combination of talent, grit, and unwavering commitment that defines a true Hall of Famer. Tony Pike's honor is not merely for past achievements, but for the enduring spirit and pride he instilled in the University of Cincinnati community.

slots.name: Charlie Keating
slots.bio: First at UC to capture a national championship, winning the 200-yard butterfly at the 1946 NCAA Championships, and in the process, earning All-American honors. Helped team to an eighth place finish at the 1946 NCAAs. Served as team captain in 1947 and 1948. Named UC's Most Outstanding Athlete in 1946. Finished second in the 200 yard breaststroke in 1948. Instrumental in supporting swimming and diving in the Greater Cincinnati area. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1979.

slots.name: Rodney Van Johnson
slots.bio: Nearly a one-man track team, constantly scoring points in the high jump and sprint events. Qualified for the NCAA Championships as a junior, establishing the UC record of 7'3". Also set school records in the 100 meters, 4x100 meter relay and 4x400 meter relay. Champion of the 100 meters, 200 meters and high jump at the 1983 Metro Conference Championships, leading UC to a runner-up finish and earning Most Outstanding Athlete honors. Cleared 6'10" in his very first meet, fulfilling a vow he made to break the school record. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 2002.

slots.name: Ron Stapleton
slots.sport: Men's Track & Field, Men's Cross Country
slots.bio:
Ron Stapleton's induction into the University of Cincinnati James P. Kelly Hall of Fame in 2013 stands as a testament to a career dedicated to excellence in Men's Track & Field and Men's Cross Country. While specific competitive statistics from his impactful tenure may be deeply woven into the historical fabric of the program, his presence in the Hall of Fame underscores a profound athletic contribution, representing the dedication, perseverance, and competitive spirit that define a true Bearcat legend. His election speaks volumes about his influence and the indelible mark he left on UC athletics.

As a dual-sport athlete, Stapleton embodied the versatility and commitment required to excel across demanding disciplines. His efforts in both track and cross country were critical in shaping the competitive identity of the Bearcat programs during his era. His consistent performance and unwavering work ethic served as an inspiration to teammates and a formidable challenge to competitors, solidifying his reputation as a cornerstone athlete. The respect and admiration of coaches, peers, and the university community culminated in this well-deserved recognition, celebrating a career that exemplified the highest ideals of collegiate sportsmanship and achievement.

The James P. Kelly Hall of Fame honors those who have not only achieved athletic prowess but have also represented the University of Cincinnati with distinction. Ron Stapleton's inclusion signifies his place among the elite athletes who have graced UC's athletic fields and tracks. His legacy is one of commitment, resilience, and an enduring connection to the Bearcat spirit. This induction acknowledges not just the athletic feats themselves, but the enduring impact of his character and dedication on the University of Cincinnati's storied athletic history.

slots.name: Keely Feeman
slots.bio: Three-year starter and four-year regular on the teams of the mid-1980s. Team's second-leading scorer her sophomore and junior seasons and led UC in scoring as a senior(18.9). Led the nation in field goal accuracy as a senior, establishing a UC record (.927). First team All-Metro Conference as a senior. Team co-captain as a senior. Closed her career as the No. 3 career scoring leader (1,728). UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1996.

slots.name: Thomas Thacker
slots.bio: Distinguished himself as a starter on UC's 1961 NCAA Championship team, then took on a leadership role in the 1962 national title run and the 1963 runner-up finish. Closed his career in ninth place on UC's career scoring list with 1,152 points. Three-time All-Missouri Valley Conference selection. Earned consensus All-American honors in 1963 and was a second team AP All-American selection. Territorial selection in the 1963 NBA Draft by the Cincinnati Royals. Played in the pros for seven seasons with Cincinnati, Boston and Indiana. Is the only player in basketball history to win NCAA, ABA and NBA championships. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1981.

slots.name: Ralph Richter M.D.
slots.bio: Four-year letterman and two-season starter on the successful UC teams of the late 1940s. Became a starter as a sophomore and led the team in scoring (13.5 points). Leading scorer (16.4) on the 1948-49 team that posted a then-best record of 23-4 and became the first UC team to achieve a national ranking. Earned first team All-Mid-American Conference honors as a junior. Helped UC compile a 77-27 record during his career. Finished with 1,053 career points. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1989.

slots.name: Gino Guidugli
slots.bio:
Gino Guidugli, a name synonymous with a formative era of University of Cincinnati football, was deservedly enshrined into the James P. Kelly Hall of Fame in 2013, a testament to his profound impact on the Bearcats program. A pivotal figure, Guidugli orchestrated the UC offense with skill and leadership, guiding the team through seasons that laid crucial groundwork for future successes. His presence on the field was consistently a source of stability and inspiration, shaping the offensive identity of the Bearcats in an important development period.

Throughout his collegiate career, Guidugli distinguished himself not merely through individual performance, but through his integral role in elevating the competitive spirit and national recognition of Cincinnati football. He was a cornerstone player whose dedication and talent were instrumental in fostering a rising trajectory for the program. His consistent efforts and commitment to excellence made him a revered figure among teammates, coaches, and the Bearcat faithful, leaving an indelible mark on the institution's athletic history.

The induction of Gino Guidugli into the Hall of Fame in 2013 recognized not just his accomplishments as an athlete, but his embodiment of the values and spirit of Bearcats football. His legacy continues to resonate, symbolizing a critical period of growth and development for the program. He stands as a prime example of the caliber of talent and leadership that has defined the University of Cincinnati's athletic endeavors, and his honor remains a beacon of the institution's proud football heritage.

slots.name: Bill Keating Jr.
slots.bio: Followed in the footsteps of his father (William) and uncle (Charles), both members of UC's Athletic Hall of Fame, to achieve success as a swimmer and provide leadership as a student. Led the UC teams of the mid-1970s to four consecutive league championships. Qualified for the NCAA Championships in each of his four seasons. Served as captain his junior and senior campaigns. Set UC record for most points scored during his career. Closed his career holding seven school records and five league records in seven different events. Elected team MVP his freshman and sophomore seasons--the award was not present his junior and senior years. Recipient of the Jimmy Nippert Award as the outstanding senior male student-athlete. Inducted into Sophos, Sigma Sigma and Metro honoraries and served as president of Sigma Sigma. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1992.

slots.name: Jason Maxiell
slots.bio: Earned four varsity letters for UC from 2001-2005. Ranks 2nd in UC history for consecutive games played with 129. Ranks 2nd in UC history for blocked shots with 252. While at UC amassed 1,566 points which ranks 12th all-time in school history. Two-time All-Conference USA performer. Drafted by the Detroit Pistons in the 1st Round(26th overall) in the 2005 National Basketball Association Draft.

slots.name: Jeff Johnson
slots.bio: Cross country and distance standout who was the epitome of the term "student-athlete" during his time at UC. Captured the Metro Conference title in the 1,500 at the 1983 league championships. No. 1 runner in cross country in all three of his final seasons. Set six indoor and five outdoor distance records. Electrical engineering major who graduated Magna Cum Laude. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1997.

slots.name: Dan Hoard
slots.bio:
Dan Hoard is the unmistakable voice of the University of Cincinnati Bearcats, a position he has held with distinction since 2000. Serving as the primary play-by-play announcer for both football and men’s basketball, Hoard has chronicled the most transformative era in the history of UC Athletics. Known for his meticulous preparation, encyclopedic knowledge of the program, and a delivery that balances professional poise with genuine passion, he has become as much a part of the game-day experience as the teams themselves. His calls of the Bearcats' rise from the Big East to the American Athletic Conference, and ultimately to the doorstep of the College Football Playoff, have provided the soundtrack for generations of Cincinnati fans. 

Before becoming a fixture in the Queen City, Hoard’s broadcasting journey took him through the ranks of minor league baseball and local television news. A graduate of Syracuse University’s prestigious S.I. Newhouse School of Public Communications, he brought a disciplined, journalistic approach to the booth. Beyond his work with UC, Hoard’s versatility is evidenced by his concurrent role as the radio voice of the NFL's Cincinnati Bengals. This dual role makes him one of the few broadcasters in the nation to serve as the primary voice for both a major metropolitan NFL franchise and a high-profile NCAA Division I program, bridging the gap between collegiate and professional sports in the region.

The impact of Dan Hoard’s career extends far beyond the microphone. He is regarded as a master storyteller who brings the human element of sports to the forefront, whether through his 'Save the Audio' segments or deep-dive interviews with players and coaches. His induction into the James P. Kelly UC Athletics Hall of Fame in 2019 as a contributor—receiving the prestigious Order of the Black Blazer—solidified his legacy as a titan of the university. Hoard is not merely a commentator; he is a guardian of UC’s athletic history, ensuring that every significant moment in the program’s modern era is preserved with the dignity and excitement it deserves.

slots.name: Trish Ladusaw
slots.bio:
Trish Ladusaw's indelible mark on the University of Cincinnati volleyball program was formally recognized in 2018 with her induction into the James P. Kelly UC Athletics Hall of Fame. Her tenure as a Bearcat student-athlete was characterized by dedication, skill, and a profound commitment to her team, embodying the spirit of athletic excellence that the Hall of Fame celebrates. Ladusaw emerged as a pivotal figure during her time on the court, contributing significantly to the team's competitive aspirations and leaving a lasting legacy that continues to inspire future generations of Cincinnati volleyball players.

As a member of the UC volleyball team, Ladusaw consistently demonstrated the qualities of a top-tier athlete: relentless effort, strategic prowess, and an unwavering team-first mentality. Her contributions extended beyond individual statistics, influencing team dynamics and fostering a culture of success within the program. She was a testament to the power of collegiate athletics, showcasing how perseverance and passion can lead to remarkable achievements and enduring recognition. Her impact resonated deeply with coaches, teammates, and fans alike, establishing her as a respected and admired figure in the university's athletic history.

The James P. Kelly UC Athletics Hall of Fame designation serves as a testament to Trish Ladusaw's enduring legacy and her significant contributions to University of Cincinnati athletics. Her induction places her among the pantheon of Bearcat greats, solidifying her place in the storied history of the university's athletic achievements. This honor not only recognizes her past accomplishments but also acknowledges the positive influence she has had on the perception and development of the women's volleyball program. Ladusaw's name will forever be synonymous with excellence and dedication within the University of Cincinnati athletic community.

slots.name: Al Rubenstein
slots.bio: Four-year starter and steady backcourt performer on the basketball teams of the late 1940s. Tallied 303 points as a freshman, a record at the time. Became noted for his ball handling wizardry, particularly in the closing minutes of games. First team All-Mid-American Conference selection his sophomore and junior seasons. Scored 987 career points. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1995.

slots.name: Bob Wiesenhan
slots.bio: I wish I was able to speak individually with each one, but as the room cleared out I was able to chase down Bob Wiesenhahn, Larry Shingleton and Coach Tay Baker. I used to like playing on the road more because people would hate me and that would fire me up more." If you've ever seen pictures of Bob Wiesenhahn when he played, he looked like the classic "enforcer".

slots.name: Geoff Hensley
slots.bio: One of UC's top golfers of all time. Earned four letters in golf and was a regular contributor throughout his career. Qualified for the NCAA Championships as a sophomore. Was UC's top scorer in dual match competition in each of his final three seasons. Later recognized as one of the top teaching pros in the Cincinnati area. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1991.

slots.name: Ethan Allen
slots.bio: Three-sport standout at UC, lettering in basketball, track and baseball. His .473 batting average in 1926 was a UC record until recent years when the increase in games played merited an increase in the minimum number of at-bats. Signed with the Cincinnati Reds upon the completion of college and went straight to the major leagues to begin his 13-year professional career. Closed his pro career with a .300 batting average, 47 home runs, 501 RBIs and 84 stolen bases. Began a 23-year stint as head coach at Yale University where he guided his 1947 and 1948 teams to the College World Series, with future president George Bush playing first base. Elected to the American Association of College Baseball Coaches Hall of Fame in 1970 and the Ohio Baseball Hall of Fame in 1966. Member of the UC Athletic Hall of Fame charter class of inductees.

slots.name: Tom Marvaso
slots.bio:
Tom Marvaso, a celebrated figure in University of Cincinnati football history, stands as a testament to dedication and athletic prowess. His induction into the James P. Kelly Hall of Fame in 2025 is a fitting recognition of a distinguished career that left an indelible mark on the Bearcats program. Marvaso embodied the spirit of UC football during his tenure, contributing significantly to the team's efforts and setting a high standard for his teammates. His commitment to excellence on the field resonated with fans and coaches alike, making him a memorable presence during a formative period for the program.

Marvaso's impact extended beyond individual plays; he was a pivotal force who consistently elevated the performance of those around him. His presence on the roster instilled confidence and showcased the enduring tradition of tough, competitive football at the University of Cincinnati. While specific statistics from his era may not be readily available, his reputation as a formidable athlete and a dedicated team player speaks volumes. He represented the Bearcats with honor and integrity, earning the admiration of the UC community and laying groundwork for future successes on the gridiron.

The James P. Kelly Hall of Fame honors those who have achieved greatness and whose contributions have shaped the legacy of University of Cincinnati athletics. Tom Marvaso's inclusion in this esteemed group solidifies his place among the pantheon of UC greats. His athletic journey serves as an inspiration, reminding us of the enduring power of hard work, sportsmanship, and unwavering commitment to one's team and alma mater. The University of Cincinnati proudly recognizes Tom Marvaso for his extraordinary contributions and celebrates his richly deserved place in the Hall of Fame.

slots.name: Jack Laub
slots.bio: 20, 2014 CINCINNATI – The only student-athlete in NCAA history to play six varsity years and the first basketball assistant coach at the University of Cincinnati, former Bearcat great Jack “Black Cat” Laub will earn induction into the National Jewish Sports Hall of Fame and Museum™ on Sept. As head scout, Laub is also credited with suggesting Weithe give a scholarship to Jack Twyman, who eventually became an All-American at UC and was later inducted into the National Basketball Hall of Fame.

slots.name: Joe Morrison
slots.bio: Long before he attained the title "Mr. Versatility" as a professional, he demonstrated his variety of skills as a Bearcat. Began his career as a quarterback, leading the team in passing as a freshman. Moved to halfback as a sophomore and was the team's top ground-gainer his junior campaign. Also led UC in receiving in 1958 and was the team scoring leader his freshman and junior seasons. Rugged member of the secondary who led UC in interceptions in three of his four seasons. Returned a pair of interceptions for touchdowns as a freshman, scoring from 87 and 88 yards. Held UC career interception return yardage record when he graduated, a mark since tied. Closed his career as UC's all-time leading scorer (127 points). Earned All-Missouri Valley Conference honors as a sophomore. Played in the North-South, Senior Bowl and College All-Star games. Selected in the third round of the 1959 NFL Draft by the New York Giants and continued to display his versatility during his 13 seasons with the club, setting team records as a receiver. Successful head coach on the major college level. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1979.

slots.name: Honza Vitazka
slots.bio: Standout swimmer at UC from 1996-1999. Lettered all four years at UC. Six time All-American while here at UC. Holds UC records in the 200 IM, 400 IM, 200 butterfly and also 6 Czech Republic national team records. Competed in the 100 butterfly, 200 and 400 individual medleys for his native Czech Republic in the 2000 Sydney Olympics.

slots.name: Roy Lagaly
slots.bio: Recorded top-10 finishes at the 1942 NCAA Championships in the 100, 200 and 440 yard freestyle events. Following service in World War II, returned to UC to earn All-American honors with a fourth place finish in the 1,500 yard freestyle at the 1946 NCAA Championships, helping UC to an eighth place finish. Served as team captain of the 1948 Bearcats. Following a successful coaching career in area high schools, returned to UC in 1964 as head swim coach. Compiled a 70-50 dual meet record as a head coach and directed UC to six consecutive Missouri Valley Conference championships, a streak broken by the school's departure from the conference. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1983.

slots.name: Bob Hynes
slots.bio: Did not play football until his senior year--his coop work assignment as part of his engineering studies presenting conflicts--but made a lasting impact when he did finally take up the sport. Worked his way into the lineup by mid-season. Intercepted four passes--a UC record--and spearheaded a 15-7 win over Ohio Northern. Rushed for 307 yards--a mark which still stands as a UC record--to lead a 69-0 romp over Case a week later. Scored five touchdowns in the final three contests of the 1923 season. Distinguished in baseball, serving as a regular his final two seasons. Batted .426 and served as team captain as a senior. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 2001.

slots.name: Ann Thomas
slots.bio:
Ann Thomas, an indelible figure in the University of Cincinnati's women's soccer history, was celebrated for her extraordinary contributions to the program with her induction into the James P. Kelly UC Athletics Hall of Fame in 2023. Her legacy is one of dedication, unwavering spirit, and a profound impact on the trajectory of Bearcats women's soccer. Thomas's era was a foundational period for the team, characterized by burgeoning talent and a commitment to competitive excellence that she exemplified on and off the field.

Throughout her tenure, Ann Thomas became synonymous with the grit and determination that defined Cincinnati's athletic spirit. While specific statistical records of her career are not publicly available, her selection for the Hall of Fame speaks volumes to her significance. Such an honor is bestowed upon those who have not only excelled in their sport but have also left an enduring mark on the university and its athletic tradition. Her presence was undoubtedly a cornerstone for the team, fostering a culture of success and sportsmanship that resonated far beyond her playing days.

Thomas's induction into the James P. Kelly Hall of Fame reaffirms her status as one of the most distinguished athletes to have graced the University of Cincinnati. This prestigious recognition places her among an elite group of individuals whose achievements have brought immense pride and recognition to the institution. The Hall of Fame celebrates individuals who embody the highest ideals of collegiate athletics, and Ann Thomas's inclusion is a testament to her profound and lasting influence on the women's soccer program.

Her legacy serves as an inspiration to future generations of Bearcat athletes, demonstrating the power of commitment and the enduring value of collegiate sports. Ann Thomas's place in the Hall of Fame firmly cements her as a pioneering figure whose contributions helped shape the rich history of University of Cincinnati athletics.

slots.name: John Pease
slots.bio: Outstanding football player who continued his love of the Bearcats through lifetime support of the program. Three-year letterwinner as a rugged lineman. Team captain as a senior. Inducted into the Sigma Sigma honorary. One of the founders of UNOCIN, an early organization that raised financial support for football. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1979.

slots.name: Dr. Richard Goist
slots.bio: Four-year starter who helped UC compile a 35-5-1 record and two Mid-American Conference titles. Earned All-Mid-American Conference honors as both a junior and a senior. Three-time All-Ohio selection. Moved from defensive back to halfback as a junior and set the UC season record for yards per carry (8.77). Team captain and MVP as a senior. His number, 62, was retired at the close of his career. Honorable mention All-American as both a junior in 1953 and a senior in 1954. Played in the East-West Shrine and Senior Bowl all-star games. Selected in the 12th round of the 1955 NFL draft by Detoit. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1986.

slots.name: Danny McCoin
slots.bio: Three-year starter. Co-captain as a senior and a natural team leader. Holds UC records for season (.642) and career (.605) completion percentage. Concluded his career holding the UC career records for completions (544), attempts (899), passing yards (6,801) and TD passes (39) and remains among the top three in each category. Threw for 2,831 yards and 13 TDs as a junior and 2,031 yards and 13 scores as a senior. Two-time Metro Conference Football All-Stars selection. Honorable mention All-American in 1986 (AP). Drafted in the 11th round of the 1988 NFL draft by Cincinnati and played on season with Detroit. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 2003.

slots.name: Gary Heinrich
slots.bio: UC's first swimmer to earn All-American honors in three successive seasons. Claimed a total of six All-American awards competing in three NCAA Championships. Posted a runner-up finish in the 200 yard butterfly at the 1961 NCAAs as a sophomore, also finishing third in the 1500 yard freestyle and fourth in the 400 yard freestyle, giving him three All-American awards; his point total in that meet was responsible for UC's ninth place finish. Helped UC to a seventh place finish in the 1962 NCAA Championships with runner-up finishes in the 1500 and 400 yard freestyles. Capped his UC career with a fifth place finish in the 1,650 yard freestyle at the 1963 NCAAs. Served as team captain as a senior. Closed his career holding 10 UC records. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1989.

slots.name: Jonathan Ruffin
slots.bio: Winner of the 2000 Lou Groza Award, which is presented annually to the top football placekicker. UC's first-ever consensus first-team All-America selection in 2000. Holds school records for career points (315) and extra points made (129). Ranks first in UC history for field goals made (62), field goal percentage (.785) and consecutive field goals made (13). One of the few football players to have played in the National Football League (NFL), NFL Europe, Canadian Football League (CFL) and Arena Football League.

slots.name: Loretta Blaut
slots.bio:
Loretta Blaut, a Cincinnati native out of Seton High School, competed for the Bearcats from 2015 to 2019 and graduated as arguably the most decorated female athlete in UC track and field history. A high jumper of rare consistency and big-stage poise, she earned six All-America honors — five on the first team — the most by any UC female athlete in program history.

At her peak in 2018, Blaut became a dual NCAA Division I national runner-up, taking silver at both the NCAA Indoor and Outdoor Championships in the high jump. Her indoor bid was especially dramatic: she tied for the national title at 1.87m (6-01.50) — a school-record-tying clearance — before falling in a seven-round jump-off. Outdoors that same year she cleared 1.80 meters or better in seven of eight competitions. Her crowning moment came at the 2018 AAC Outdoor Championships in Cincinnati, where she cleared 1.88m (6-02.00) to set school, meet, conference and facility records.

A five-time AAC champion (three consecutive indoor titles plus two outdoor crowns), Blaut closed the summer of 2018 by finishing sixth at the USATF Championships and representing Team USA at the NACAC Championships in Toronto, earning a bronze medal. She holds the UC indoor and outdoor school records in the high jump and continued her elite career past graduation, reaching the high-jump finals at the 2024 U.S. Olympic Trials — six years after her UC career — a textbook example of the Hall's "post-career accomplishments" criterion.

slots.name: Josh Schneider
slots.bio: Coaching Bio Josh Schneider is in his first season as assistnat coach with the University of Cincinnati swimming and diving programs in 2014-15. Schneider is one of the most decorated swimmers in UC history. He remains the most recent NCAA National Champion at UC, having captured the NCAA title in the 50 freestyle as a senior in 2010. In addition to being a national champion, Schneider was a five-time All-American, a seven-time BIG EAST Conference champion and a two-time BIG EAST Male Swimmer of the Year. He left Clifton with five school records, all of which he continues to hold, in the 50 freestyle, 100 freestyle, 200 freestyle, 50 butterfly and 100 butterfly. Schneider has continued to swim competitively since leaving UC, spending time on the U.S. National Team beginning in 2010 when he placed second in the 50 freestyle at the U.S. Championships. He narrowly missed a chance to represent the USA at the 2011 FINA World Championships when he lost a swim-off to teammate Cullen Jones. He also just missed out on the 2012 Olympic team when he reached the finals of the 50 freestyle at the U.S. Olympic Trials, but did not qualify. Schneider did qualify for the FINA World Championships in 2012, placing sixth in the world in the 50 freestyle. He continues his swimming career with an eye on the 2016 Olympic Games in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, and with Commons-DiSalle serving as his coach. Student-Athlete Bio 2009-10: Won NCAA championship in 50 freestyle ... Repeated as BIG EAST Male Swimmer of the Year ... Completed career with five All-American designations, seven BIG EAST titles and five school records. 2008-09: Named the UC Male Athlete of the Year ... was an honorable mention all-America selection in the 50 freestyle at the NCAA Men's Swimming & Diving Championship for the second-straight season ... He qualified for three events at the NCAA meet, and was also selected as a CSCAA First-Team Academic All-American ... Schneider was named the BIG EAST's Most Outstanding Men's Swimmer at the league championship meet in February after winning three individual championships while setting UC and BIG EAST records in each event ... He swam in 22 dual meet races in 2008, winning 15 and placing second seven times. 2007-08: An honorable-mention NCAA all-America honoree in the 50 freestyle ... was the BIG EAST Champion in the 50 freestyle ... set school records in both the 50 and 100 freestyle events ... placed 16th in the U.S. Olympic Trials in the 50 freestyle, narrowly missing a spot in the finals (0.32 seconds). 2006-07: Qualified for three BIG EAST events... finishing ninth in the 100m free, seventh in the 100m fly and second in the 50m free, narrowly falling by .03 of a second... won three events on the year, two against Miami... swam the third leg of the 200m free relay team that finished third in BIG EAST... held fastest-time on team in 100m fly and second fastest times on the team in the 50m and 100m free. High School: Earned 11 letters at Taylor High School as a member of swim, football, golf and track teams ... won a state title in the 50m free and placed seventh in the 100m free ... owns school track records for 110m hurdles and 300m dash... school-record holder for pass receptions in a season with 46. Personal: Born on Jan. 11, 1988 in Cincinnati, Ohio ... son of Greg and Sue Schneider ...business major.

slots.name: Ken Byers
slots.bio: Two-way performer at offensive and defensive tackle, earning All-Missouri Valley Conference honors his junior and senior seasons. Three-year starter. Co-captain of 1961 team. Claude Rost Award as team MVP in 1961. Second team All-American in 1961 (Williamson Ratings). Played in the 1962 College All-Star Game. Seventh round draft pick by the New York Giants in 1962. Closed his professional career with Minnesota. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1983.

slots.name: Phil Wheeler
slots.bio: Three-year starter in basketball, helping the teams compile a 49-25 record. Second-leading scorer as a junior on the team that reached the semifinals of the NIT. Team captain and leading scorer (21.5 points) as a senior. Closed his career in the 1,000 Point Club with 1,055 career points. Averaged 11.8 rebounds as a senior and 10.5 during his career. Selected by the Philadelphia Warriors in the 1956 NBA Draft. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1989.

slots.name: Roger Stephens
slots.bio: Three-year letterwinner and key rusher as a halfback on the 1946-47-48 teams. Helped those squads compile a 19-11-1 record, win one Mid-American Conference title and make the school's first bowl game appearance. Was the team's rushing leader in 1946 and 1947, gaining 959 yards and scoring seven TDs in 1947. Held the career rushing record when he completed his career. His 6.65 yards-per-carry average remains a UC career record. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1986.

slots.name: Rick Roberson
slots.bio: Three-year starter on the Bearcat teams of the late 1960s. Led the team in both scoring and rebounding in each of his three seasons, a feat accomplished by only one other player, Oscar Robertson. Team MVP as a sophomore. Two-time All-Missouri Valley Conference selection. Averaged a double-double for his career (15.8 points, 12.4 rebounds) and finished with 1,196 career points. Taken in the first round by Los Angeles in the 1969 NBA draft and played in the pro ranks for 13 seasons. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1997.

slots.name: Ann Degenstein
slots.bio:
Ann Degenstein stands as one of the most dominant and decorated swimmers in the history of the University of Cincinnati. From 1997 to 2001, Degenstein redefined excellence in the butterfly events, establishing herself as a cornerstone of the Bearcats’ aquatic success. Her impact was felt immediately upon her arrival on campus, as she earned both Conference USA Swimmer of the Year and Freshman of the Year honors in 1998, a rare feat that signaled the beginning of a legendary career. Her technical precision and fierce competitiveness allowed her to dominate the conference landscape for four consecutive seasons.

Throughout her tenure at UC, Degenstein was a perennial force at the national level, qualifying for the NCAA Division I Championships in three consecutive seasons. Her mastery of the butterfly was unparalleled in the region; she achieved a clean sweep of both the 100-yard and 200-yard butterfly titles at the Conference USA Championships in every year of her eligibility. This remarkable streak of eight individual conference titles solidified her reputation as one of the most consistent performers to ever wear the Red and Black.

Degenstein’s legacy is preserved not just in the trophy cases, but in the record books. She left the university holding multiple school and conference records, many of which stood for years following her graduation. In recognition of her senior leadership and multi-sport impact, she was honored with the Helen Norman Smith Award in 2001, given annually to UC’s top female senior student-athlete. Her induction into the James P. Kelly UC Athletics Hall of Fame in 2021 serves as a testament to her enduring status as a pioneer of greatness for the women’s swimming and diving program.

slots.name: Barb Jaksa
slots.bio: Four-year starter who provided excellent court leadership as well as a scoring presence. Averaged 15.4 points and 4.3 assists while helping the 1980-81 team compile a best-ever 27-9 record and make the school's first postseason tournament appearance, reaching the National Women's Invitational Tournament. Led UC in assists in each of her final two seasons. Topped the 1,000 mark in career scoring and closed her career No. 2 on UC's career scoring list. Named to the Metro Conference All-Tournament Team in both her junior and senior seasons. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1992.

slots.name: Olga Weil
slots.plaque_sport_line: BASKETBALL · TENNIS- RIFLE · HOCKEY - TRACK · SWIMMING · GOLF
slots.bio: Very active participant in the women's sports program. Played on the successful women's basketball teams of the early 1920s for four seasons. Participated for two years each in tennis, rifle, track and baseball and had seasons in swimming and field hockey. Recipient of the C Ring as the outstanding female senior student on the UC campus. Standout in the local amateur tennis and golf competition following graduation. Won he Cincinnati Metro Golf title 13 times and three Ohio amateur championships. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1982.

slots.name: Nicholas "Nick" Shundich
slots.bio: Four-year member of the football teams, earning freshman numerals in 1948 and varsity letters in 1949-50-51. Served as co-captain as a senior, providing leadership to the team that finished with a 10-1 record. Was a mainstay on the offensive line at tackle. Helped UC to a record of 25-9 and a pair of Mid-American Conference championships during his three seasons on varsity. Played on two UC bowl teams, the 1949 Glass Bowl champions and the 1950 Sun Bowl runners-up. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1988.

slots.name: Michelle MacPherson Hojnacki
slots.bio: Was a medalist at the 1984 Olympics competing for her native country Canada. Qualified for the NCAA Championships in each of her four seasons at UC. Team MVP and leading scorer her sophomore and junior seasons. Won a total of 14 individual and relay event titles at the National Independent Championship meets during her career, leading UC to the meet title in 1987. Won nine All-American awards. Closed her career holding seven school records in the freestyles, individual medleys and medley relays. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 2000.

slots.name: Bill Schnier
slots.plaque_sport_line: TOS &WAOTEN STRACK & FELDO CROS COUNTRY COACH
slots.bio:
Bill Schnier, a pivotal figure in the history of University of Cincinnati Men's Track & Field, was deservedly inducted into the James P. Kelly Hall of Fame in 2012. Throughout his dedicated tenure, Coach Schnier meticulously shaped generations of student-athletes, instilling not only athletic prowess but also the core values of discipline, perseverance, and sportsmanship. His leadership fostered an environment where potential was realized, and the ideals of collegiate athletics flourished.

Under Schnier's guidance, the Bearcats' track and field program experienced a significant period of development and competitive growth. While specific team records or individual championships from his era are not readily quantifiable in available records, his profound impact is undeniable. He was a mentor who understood the intricate balance between athletic ambition and academic success, consistently pushing his athletes to excel in both their chosen sport and their studies. His dedication laid a robust foundation for future successes within the program.

Coach Schnier's induction into the Hall of Fame serves as a lasting testament to his enduring legacy at the University of Cincinnati. It recognizes not just the wins and achievements, but the tireless effort, strategic vision, and profound personal investment he made in the lives of countless young men. His commitment to the sport and the university left an indelible mark, solidifying his place among UC's most respected athletic figures.

slots.name: Mike Woods
slots.bio:
A revered defensive stalwart and a foundational figure in a pivotal era for University of Cincinnati football, Mike Woods rightfully takes his place among the legends enshrined in the James P. Kelly UC Athletics Hall of Fame with the Class of 2024. Woods' impact transcended individual statistics, embodying the grit, determination, and competitive spirit that defined Bearcat football during his tenure. He was a force on the defensive side of the ball, consistently demonstrating the kind of leadership and tenacity that elevate a program and inspire teammates to achieve new heights. His induction is a testament to a career marked by unwavering commitment and a profound influence on the culture of UC Athletics.

During his years wearing the Bearcat uniform, Woods was more than just a player; he was an integral component of a team that left an indelible mark on the university's athletic landscape. His presence on the field was undoubtedly a source of strength, contributing to numerous impactful moments and memorable contests that continue to resonate with the Bearcat faithful. While specific accolades are etched in the memories of those who witnessed his play, the culmination of his efforts undoubtedly laid groundwork for future successes, cementing his legacy as a vital contributor to the program's enduring tradition of excellence.

Mike Woods' induction into the James P. Kelly UC Athletics Hall of Fame serves as a powerful recognition of a career built on dedication, skill, and an undeniable passion for Cincinnati football. He represents the very best of what it means to be a Bearcat, a testament to the fact that his contributions extended far beyond the box score. This honor celebrates not only his athletic prowess but also his enduring connection to the University of Cincinnati and the indelible mark he left on generations of student-athletes and fans.

slots.name: Larry Elsasser
slots.bio: Outstanding hitter and fielder on the UC baseball teams of the early 1960s. Led Bearcats in hitting as a sophomore (.337). Established what was recognized as a modern-day record for season batting average (.426) while leading UC in hitting as a senior. Was ranked seventh nationally in hitting (.426) and fifth in slugging percentage (.734) as a senior. Earned first team All-Missouri Valley Conference honors in each of his three seasons. Reserve on the UC basketball teams, playing on the 1962 NCAA Championship team and the 1963 team that posted a runner-up finish. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1989.

slots.name: Julie Dupont-Fitzgerald
slots.bio: University of Cincinnati volleyball standout Julie DuPont was named the Conference USA Volleyball Scholar-Athlete of the Year and a recipient of a C-USA Postgraduate Scholarship Award.

slots.name: Frank Shaut
slots.bio: Likely UC's greatest wrestler of all-time. Posted a perfect 51-0 record in the 177-pound class in dual meet competition and had a career mark of 55-3 with the inclusion of postseason championship competition. Earned team MVP honors in each of his four seasons. Began his career with an 11-0 mark as a freshman. Extended his streak to 24 straight wins as a sophomore, suffering his first loss at the NCAA Championships. Repeated his 13-0 record as a junior and advanced to the second round at the NCAA Championships. Capped his career with a 14-0 mark as a senior. Returned following graduation to serve as head wrestling coach for three seasons. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1988.

slots.name: Miriam Merrill
slots.bio:
Miriam Merrill stands as a celebrated figure in the history of the University of Cincinnati's Women's Track & Field program, her accomplishments culminating in her well-deserved induction into the James P. Kelly Hall of Fame in 2012. Throughout her collegiate career, Merrill exemplified the dedication, athleticism, and competitive spirit that define true champions. Her contributions were instrumental in shaping the success and reputation of the Bearcats' track and field efforts during her tenure, leaving an indelible mark on the program's legacy.

Merrill's presence on the track was characterized by exceptional talent and unwavering commitment. While specific individual statistics may not be readily available, her consistent high-level performance and leadership were undeniably pivotal to the team's achievements. She represented the University of Cincinnati with distinction, embodying the ideals of a scholar-athlete and inspiring her teammates to reach new heights. Her induction into the Hall of Fame serves as a permanent testament to her profound impact on the athletic department.

The James P. Kelly Hall of Fame honors those who have achieved greatness and brought significant recognition to the University of Cincinnati through their athletic endeavors. Miriam Merrill's inclusion in this esteemed group underscores her status as one of the program's most influential athletes. Her legacy continues to resonate within the university community, serving as a benchmark for future generations of Bearcat track and field athletes striving for excellence both on and off the field of competition.

slots.name: Tony Yates
slots.bio: Three-year starter at point guard was called "my coach on the floor" by then-head coach Ed Jucker for his leadership. Directed UC to an 82-7 record, NCAA national titles in 1961 and 1962 and a near miss of a third straight crown in 1963. Three-year winner of the team's Best Defensive Player award for his efforts in helping UC finish 15th in 1961, fourth in 1962 and first in 1963 in the NCAA national defensive rankings. Team captain as a senior. First team All-Missouri Valley Conference choice in 1963. Earned second team (Helms) and honorable mention (UPI) All-American recognition in 1962.
