During an era when women's athletics were gaining increasing prominence, Scott stood out as a beacon of excellence. slots.name: Charles Mileham
slots.bio: Governed the emergence of UC's athletics program to national notoriety during his tenure as athletics director. Came to UC in 1926, and for 11 years served as an instructor in Physical Education, freshman football coach, varsity track head coach and director of intramurals. Became athletics director in 1936, beginning a 24-year tenure, the longest in UC history. By building schedules of regional and national power teams, he raised the level of football and basketball, football making three bowl appearances in the 1940s and 1950s and basketball becoming a regular fixture in postseason tournaments by the conclusion of his career. Oversaw the expansion of Nippert Stadium, whose capacity was increased twice during his tenure, and the construction of Armory Fieldhouse as a home arena for basketball. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1978.

slots.name: Mary Danner Wineberg
slots.bio: Mary Wineberg is in her fifth season as a volunteer assistant coach for the University of Cincinnati track program. Wineberg's responsibilities range from assisting with recruiting, and working on the development of both the men's and women's sprinters. While competing for the Bearcats as a student-athlete, Wineberg set the school record in the 400-meter dash with a time of 53.30 and placed as high as second place in the Conference USA Championships. Since graduating with a B.S. in education from UC in 2002, Wineberg has gone on to compete at the World level. Wineberg represented Team USA at the 2008 Olympics in Beijing where she won Olympic Gold as the lead off runner of the USA 4x400m relay. Alongside her success at the Olympics, Wineberg has also acquired a silver and bronze medal on the national stage. Wineberg has been ranked as high as 8th in the World in the 400m dash. In July of 2009, Wineberg was one of three athletes selected for induction as the Class of 2010 into the James P. Kelly, Sr. University of Cincinnati Athletics Hall of Fame. After the Olympic Games, Wineberg took 2009 off from running to start a family. She gave birth to her daughter Brooklyn on August 3, 2009. Just 1 month later, Wineberg began training was on the comeback trail. Less than one year later, Wineberg finished in the top ten in the nation at USA Outdoor Nationals. She continues her training with her sights set on the 2012 Olympics. She is married to sprints coach Chris Wineberg. The couple welcomed a daughter, Brooklyn, in August 2009.

slots.name: Angie Trostel

Qualified for the 1996 Olympic Trials and narrowly missed a berth on the U.S. Team. Champion of both the one-meter and three-meter events at the National Independent Championships as a sophomore and earned All-American honors in both events at the NCAA Championships. Earned two more All-American awards as a junior and capped her career with a pair of All-American finishes as a senior. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 2006.

slots.name: Jason Kelce
slots.bio:
Jason Daniel Kelce (born November 5, 1987, Cleveland Heights, Ohio) is the most decorated professional athlete in University of Cincinnati football history. He arrived at UC in 2006 as a non-recruited walk-on linebacker, converted to offensive line during the program's transition years, and started for both back-to-back BIG EAST championship teams before being selected in the sixth round of the 2011 NFL Draft and authoring a 13-season Hall-of-Fame-caliber career with the Philadelphia Eagles.

As a true freshman in 2006, Kelce was named the program's Scout Team Defensive MVP. He moved to the offensive line in 2007, redshirted while learning the new position, and emerged as a starter in 2008. He started on the offensive line for both the 2008 and 2009 BIG EAST championship teams — appearing in the FedEx Orange Bowl (January 2009 vs. Virginia Tech) and the Allstate Sugar Bowl (January 2010 vs. Florida) — and earned All–BIG EAST recognition in both 2009 and 2010. His younger brother Travis Kelce would follow him to UC two years later as a scholarship tight end.

The Philadelphia Eagles selected Kelce 191st overall in the sixth round of the 2011 NFL Draft. He started at center as a rookie and never relinquished the position. Across 13 seasons (2011–2023) he was named First-Team All-Pro six times (2014, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2021, 2023), selected to the Pro Bowl seven times, played in two Super Bowls (LII and LVII), and won Super Bowl LII over the New England Patriots. He set the Eagles franchise record with 156 consecutive regular-season starts and finished second in Eagles franchise history with 193 career games played. At his retirement on March 4, 2024, his six First-Team All-Pro selections tied the Eagles franchise record alongside Pro Football Hall of Famers Reggie White and Chuck Bednarik. In his final season at age 36, his 80.7 Pro Football Focus grade made him the highest-graded center who played 1,000 snaps.

Kelce co-hosts the New Heights podcast with brother Travis — one of the most listened-to sports podcasts in the world — and in 2019 established the Kelce Brothers Scholarship at UC, directly benefiting current UC student-athletes. He is widely considered a certain first-ballot Pro Football Hall of Famer.

slots.name: Jack Twyman
slots.bio: Persistence--he was cut from his high school team three times--not only landed him a spot on the varsity as a senior but launched a career that took him to college and professional stardom and a place in the National Basketball Hall of Fame. Impressive play on the junior varsity earned him a berth on the varsity midway through his freshman season at UC. Led the team in scoring and rebounding in each of his final three seasons, averaging 24.6 points and 16.5 rebounds as a senior. Concluded his career as UC's all-time scoring (1,598) and rebounding (1,242) leader, achieving totals which five decades later rank eighth and second, respectively. Earned second team All-American honors in 1955 (NEA, International News Service, Tempo) and was an honorable mention choice by Converse. Taken by the Rochester Royals in the 1955 NBA draft, embarking on an 11-season NBA career. Was named the the NBA All-Star Team in six of his 11 seasons and led the league in scoring with his 31.2 average in 1959-60. Became the legal guardian of Royals teammate Maurice Stokes, who was stricken by a stroke at the end of the 1958 season, and helped raise money to defray Stokes' medical expenses. Charter member of the UC Athletics Hall of Fame. Elected to the National Basketball Hall of Fame in 1982. His jersey No. 27 was retired by UC in 1993.

Veteran who served in World War I, and helped train the troops who were doing their training at UC during World War II. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 2003.

slots.name: Jim Herman
slots.bio: Former University of Cincinnati golfer Jim Herman won his third PGA Tour event on Sunday, taking the top spot in the Wyndham Championship in Greensboro, N.C. Herman shot 66-69-61-63=259 to finish 21-under, a one-stroke lead over Billy Horschel at Sedgefield Country Club. He shot three straight birdies on Friday to make the cut then rose from four strokes off the lead to win the event on an exciting Sunday. Since earning his PGA Tour card in November of 2010, the former Bearcats golfer has won three PGA events. Herman won the Shell Houston Open in 2016 and the Barbasol Championship in July 2019. The win at the Wyndham Championship now puts him in contention for the FedEx Cup Playoffs. Herman played at UC from 1996-2000 before turning pro in 2000. He is currently exempt through the 2023 season and sits at No. 54 in the FedEx Cup leaderboard with invites to the first two events of the playoffs. He also secured a trip to the 2021 Masters with the victory.

slots.name: Ed Jucker
slots.bio: Lettered in baseball and basketball. Served as captain and co-leading scorer of the 1939-40 basketball team. Helped recruit future Hall of Famer Sandy Koufax to UC on a basketball scholarship and also coached future pros Mike Hershberger and Carl Bouldin. Guided UC to its first NCAA Tournament appearance in baseball in 1956. Became head basketball coach in 1960-61 and directed UC to NCAA national championships in each of his first two seasons, and a near miss of a then-unprecedented third straight title in an overtime loss in the 1963 NCAA championship game. Won national coach of the year honors in each of his three seasons. Compiled a 113-28 record in five seasons and his .801 winning percentage is the top among all UC head coaches. His .917 winning percentage in the NCAA Tournament is still a national record. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1978.

slots.name: Cliff Goldmeyer
slots.bio: Two-way standout on the 1929-30-31 football teams, playing fullback and linebacker and also handled the punting. Earned All-Ohio honors. Inducted into the ULEX and Sigma Sigma honoraries. Served one season as an assistant football coach. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1987.

Silver medalist at the 2008 Beijing Olympics in the 110m hurdles.

Second team All-American in 1970 (Central Press), third team selection (AP). UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1990.

slots.name: Kevin Youkilis

Played in the Cape Cod Collegiate Baseball League where he finished the summer 6th in batting average. Drafted in the 8th Round(243rd pick)of the 2001 MLB First -Year Amateur Draft by the Boston Red Sox. 2002 Boston Red Sox Minor League Player of the Year. Two-time World Series Champion and three-time All-Star with the Boston Red Sox.

slots.name: Miller Huggins
slots.bio: Captain of the 1900 UC baseball team and played a key role as a player and organizer of the school's baseball teams at the turn of the century. Embarked on a 13-season career in the professional ranks, playing for the Cincinnati Reds (1904-09) and the St. Louis Cardinals (1910-16), finishing with a lifetime batting average of .265. Served as player-manager of the Cardinals beginning in 1913. Became manager of the New York Yankees in 1918, where during his 12 seasons he coached the Bronx Bombers to six American League pennants and three World Series titles. Elected to the Baseball Hall of Fame in 1964. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 1977.

slots.name: John Wiethe
slots.bio: Credited with bringing Bearcat basketball to a national stature during his tenure as head coach. Fiery style meshed well with the older players who were returning to school following service in World War II. In his initial year (1946-47), directed UC, which had had one winning season in the previous seven campaigns, to a 17-9 record and the first of five straight Mid-American Conference titles. Guided the 1948-49 team to the school's first 20-win season with a 23-5 ledger and a ranking in the national polls. His 1950-51 Bearcats made the school's first postseason tourney appearance, advancing to the NIT. Concluded his six-season career with a 106-47 record. Practicing attorney who became a major figure in Cincinnati-area politics. UC Athletic Hall of Fame 2006.
